plan.notes: Transcribed from the official ARC 'Music AA-T Degree - guitarist/pianist/composer (Full Time, Fall Start)' program roadmap, Catalog 2026-27, published July 15, 2026 (mapmaker.losrios.edu/Maps/7362/PublishedPdf), GE Pattern: Cal-GETC. Total Units 61 = 16+15+14+16 (semester sums verified). tccns mirrors ARC local course codes (California community colleges do not use TCCNS). Performance courses: students are expected to take a minimum of 8 units from MUP 310, 311, 320, 321, 323, 324, 330, 331, 340, 341, 350, 352, 360, 361, 400, or 401 (which courses are used depends on the student's concentration). Large performance ensemble courses carry an enrollment limitation: the ability to play at least one instrument commonly used in the ensemble. Students can substitute ESLW 340 for ENGL C1000/C1000H. B.A./B.M. programs often require a music history course like MUFHL 310 — discuss B.A./B.M. options with Music department faculty or staff. Scheduling: MUFHL 310, 400 and 410 are offered in the fall; MUFHL 401 and 411 are offered in the spring. Most CSUs require an entry piano proficiency demonstration. The Area 5C (Science Lab) course must correspond with either the Area 5A or Area 5B course and must be taken concurrently or after the lecture course. The CSU system requires every bachelor's degree student to be knowledgeable about the U.S. Constitution, American history, and state and local government (American Institutions); students can complete this requirement at ARC before transferring.
